hints: Look carefully at which side of the diagram is the anatomical right and left of the heart, and notice whether labels B and C point to upper thin-walled chambers or lower thick-walled chambers.
Remember that the aorta is the large central arch leaving the left ventricle, while the pulmonary arteries branch to the left and right lungs, so check what vessel A is actually pointing to.
walkthrough:
**Orient yourself to the heart section**

Think of this as looking at someone facing you, so their right is on your left. That means the chambers on the left side of the page are the right atrium and right ventricle, and the chambers on the right side of the page are the left atrium and left ventricle.

**Identify the chambers and great vessels**

Atria are the smaller upper receiving chambers, ventricles are the larger lower pumping chambers with valves and tendinous cords. The aorta is the big central arch on top that curves back and gives off head and arm branches, while the pulmonary trunk sits in front and splits to the lungs.

**Check each label**

Label C on the left of the page points to the upper right-side chamber, which is the right atrium. Label B on the right of the page points to the upper left-side chamber, so it is the left atrium not the left ventricle. Label D points to the aorta in the centre, and label A points to a branch of the aortic arch, not the pulmonary artery.

options.A: Label A points to a branch of the aortic arch going to the upper body, not the pulmonary artery which branches toward the lungs.
options.B: Label B points to the left atrium, the upper chamber on the anatomical left, not the thick-walled left ventricle below it.
options.C: Label C correctly points to the right atrium, the upper receiving chamber on the anatomical right side of the heart.
options.D: Label D points to the pulmonary trunk and pulmonary artery leaving the right ventricle, not the central aortic arch leaving the left ventricle.
